conversation:
maria: FYI saw a cluster-level uptick in Xid and ECC warnings in us-west-2 overnight, ~0.8% of cards reporting transient ECC corrections.
aj: ugh, is that correlated with the 2027-06-08 firmware push? saw a few canaries flake yesterday.
maria: yes, all affected hosts are on gpu-fw v4.3.2; non-upgraded hosts are clean.
devon: do we have detail on action type? ECC corrected vs uncorrected vs Xid59? need to know drain urgency.
maria: mostly corrected ECC w/ occasional Xid 31/43 on restart. logs show PCI resets then device disappears for ~10-30s.
sre_lead: timeline? how many cards, how many hosts?
maria: ~12 cards across 8 hosts (~0.6% of fleet in that region). but cluster load was high during window.
cal: small numbers but I worry about correlated failure during peak sustained batches.
aj: agree. we should assess spare pool headroom if we had a burst of simultaneous drains.
devon: quick calc: current us-west-2 GPU count = 2000 cards. baseline observed monthly failure_rate = 0.5% historically -> ~10 cards/month. this event spikes short-term to ~0.8% -> ~16 cards. expected concurrent drains depends on MTTR.
maria: MTTR for a drain+replace is ~45min avg (drain 10m + reprovision/replace 35m). with sustained bursts we could see 20-30 concurrent drains.
aj: proposal: increase regional hot spare ratio from 2% -> 3.5% for 72 hours while we roll back or patch fw. that gives us +30 cards in region.
cal: cost tradeoff: 1% spare in us-west-2 =~ 20 cards. monthly cost per card (amortized infra) = $120 -> 20*$120 = $2400/month. bump to 3.5% is +50 cards -> +$6000/month. temporary 72h bump is negligible.
sre_lead: temporary bump makes sense. but we should also tweak autoscaler thresholds to prefer non-affected AZs and avoid scheduling large batches in the region.
devon: ops runbook suggestion: 1) roll fw revert for remaining hosts 2) mark affected hosts cordon/drain 3) increase spare pool and pre-warm images on spares 4) monitor ECC/Xid rate for 24h 5) if persistent, escalate to HW RMA for cards with repeated Xid traces.
maria: added a quick sensor query:
```
-- estimate concurrent drains
SELECT count(*) FROM gpu_events
WHERE event IN ('ecc_corrected','xid_restart')
AND ts > now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY host
HAVING count(*) > 1;
```
aj: nice. I'll add an alert threshold: if >0.5% of cards in region emit Xid in 15m -> page oncall + auto-increase spare pool.
ops-bot: alert created: gpu.xid_spike_us_west_2 threshold=0.5%/15m -> notify #eng-oncall, create incident.
cal: what about draining strategy? full node drain vs evict single GPU?
devon: for flakiness that disappears after reset we'll prefer per-GPU isolate first (nvidia-smi setcc/persistence off) then node drain if multiple GPUs degrade. avoids unnecessary node-level capacity loss.
sre_lead: decision: implement temporary spare bump + autoscaler tweak + targeted cordons. maria/aj/devon own rollout. cal will run cost impact postmortem.
maria: assigning tasks: aj -> automations for spare bump + autoscaler change (ETA 30m). devon -> patch revert plan + per-host checklist (ETA 1h). cal -> cost estimate + postmortem template (ETA EOD). I'll coordinate tracking in the incident thread.
aj: done. pushing a config change now: /configs/spare_ratio/us-west-2 -> 0.035 (temp) and autoscaler -> weight non-affected AZs + reduce max_batch_size to 90%.
ops-bot: config change applied to staging; will promote to prod on confirmation.
maria: rolling revert started on a small canary host (host-az2-114). monitoring logs.
aj: canary looks good at +20h — no Xid on reverted host. starting regional rollback at low-traffic window in 15m.
cal: note for postmortem: categorize as "firmware-related transient ECC spike" and consider quarterly fw staging for GPUs.
devon: also add kernel/pci error counters to node health export, we had noisy resets that didn't surface in current metrics.
sre_lead: agreed. next steps documented. thanks team. :thumbsup:

aj: thx all.
